abstract: Integral feedback enables perfect adaptation, but antithetic implementations can be slow and noisy. Filo et al. show that sensor-based antithetic integral feedback (sAIF) control yields effective proportional-integral (PI) behavior without adding a separate proportional module. Implemented in E. coli using split inteins, it improves disturbance rejection and noise in defined regimes.
